findings.title: Destruction of the `SmartAccount` implementation
findings.mapping_rationale: uninitialised implementation can be initialised then selfdestructed via delegatecall. A proxy-pattern defect, not an account-abstraction obligation. Generic analysers and the standard UUPS checklist cover it.

findings.title: Theft of funds under relaying the transaction
findings.mapping_rationale: calldata-length manipulation inflates the relayer refund. Gas accounting in a Safe-style execTransaction path, unrelated to the 4337 validation phase.

findings.title: Attacker can gain control of counterfactual wallet
findings.mapping_rationale: an attacker front-runs deployment of a counterfactual wallet and controls the resulting account. Maps to the deployment-initialisation obligation: initialisation must be bound to the address derivation.

findings.title: Arbitrary transactions possible due to insufficient signature validation
findings.mapping_rationale: signature validation can be evaded, permitting arbitrary transactions including implementation upgrade. The recovery result is not adequately constrained.

findings.title: Paymaster ETH can be drained with malicious sender
findings.mapping_rationale: a verifying paymaster signature is replayed after the sender upgrades to a malicious account. The sponsor digest is not bound to the sender's code or state, so sponsorship transfers to a different account behaviour.

findings.title: `FeeRefund.tokenGasPriceFactor` is not included in signed transaction data allowing the submitter to steal funds
findings.mapping_rationale: tokenGasPriceFactor is submitter-chosen and excluded from the signed data, so the submitter inflates their own refund. Directly the gas-field commitment obligation.

findings.title: Replay attack (EIP712 signed transaction)
findings.mapping_rationale: the contract checks nonces[batchId] but not batchId itself, so a signature valid in one batch replays in any batch whose nonce matches. Nonce commitment is incomplete.

findings.title: Griefing attacks on `handleOps` and `multiSend` logic
findings.mapping_rationale: front-running handleOps so a bundle reverts. A bundler-side economic attack, outside the contract-side obligation set.

findings.title: Non-compliance with EIP-4337
findings.mapping_rationale: the finding is against a modified EntryPoint's _createSenderIfNeeded, not against an account or paymaster. Out of scope: our inventory constrains accounts and paymasters, not EntryPoint forks.

findings.title: Cross-Chain Signature Replay Attack
findings.mapping_rationale: the paymaster's getHash omits chainId, so a sponsorship signature replays on every chain sharing the verifyingSigner. This is the same obligation Coinbase_SmartWallet and ZeroDev_Kernel deliberately do not meet for cross-chain owner sync; here it is an unintended defect.

findings.title: Methods used by EntryPoint has `onlyOwner` modifier
findings.mapping_rationale: execute and executeBatch carry onlyOwner in addition to _requireFromEntryPointOrOwner, so the EntryPoint cannot call them. A functional access-control mistake rather than an obligation violation.

findings.title: DoS of user operations and loss of user transaction fee due to insufficient gas value submission by malicious bundler
findings.mapping_rationale: a malicious bundler submits insufficient gas causing DoS. Bundler-side; our OP-020 constrains the account's own out-of-gas revert, not a bundler's gas choice.

findings.title: Doesn't Follow ERC1271 Standard
findings.mapping_rationale: the magic value is 0x20c13b0b with signature isValidSignature(bytes,bytes) rather than the ERC-1271 0x1626ba7e over (bytes32,bytes). The handler never returns the correct magic value.

findings.title: `SmartAccount.sol` is intended to be upgradable but inherits from contracts that contain storage and no gaps
findings.mapping_rationale: inherited contracts hold storage without gaps, risking collision on upgrade. Generic upgradeability, not an AA obligation.

findings.title: Transaction can fail due to batchId collision
findings.mapping_rationale: two execution paths share a batchId space, so nonces collide between the EntryPoint path and execTransaction. A nonce-domain defect adjacent to H-07; recorded separately because the mechanism differs.

findings.title: Remove owner calls can be replayed to remove a different owner at the same index, leading to severe issues when combined with lack of last owner guard
findings.mapping_rationale: removeOwnerAtIndex replayed via executeWithoutChainIdValidation removes a different owner on another chain because owner indices diverge, and there is no last-owner guard. Combines the chainless-digest feature (DIG-001, which we labelled applicable_absent-by-design on this contract) with the missing last-owner guard. The fix added removeLastOwner and an owner-bytes argument, which is why our D1 labelling of the current commit shows MOD-006 enforced.

findings.title: Balance check during `MagicSpend` validation cannot ensure that `MagicSpend` has enough balance to cover the requested fund
findings.mapping_rationale: MagicSpend checks its balance during validation, but the EntryPoint validates every operation in a bundle before executing any, so two operations both pass the balance check and the second cannot be funded. This is the bundle-ordering obligation, and it is the same shape as the CouponPaymaster fixture defect.

findings.title: Users can front run the signature of the paymaster operation leading to some problems
findings.mapping_rationale: a paymaster signature can be front-run and used by another sender. Sender binding on the sponsorship digest.

findings.title: Fallback handlers can trick users into calling functions of the AmbireAccount contract
findings.mapping_rationale: a fallback handler can be crafted whose selector clashes with a base AmbireAccount function, so calling the innocuous-looking handler function actually triggers the base function, including setAddrPrivilege. Maps to the fallback-forwarding obligation: a handler must be dispatched in a way that cannot be confused with the account's own selectors. Note ZeroDev_Kernel carries the same class of risk, documented in-source at L244-247 and labelled applicable_absent in D1.

findings.title: Attacker can force the failure of transactions that use `tryCatch`
findings.mapping_rationale: a relayer chooses a gas limit so the inner tryCatch call runs out of gas under the EIP-150 63/64 rule while the outer call succeeds. A gas-forwarding attack in a relayer path, not an obligation on the validation phase.

findings.title: Recovery transaction can be replayed after a cancellation
findings.mapping_rationale: the nonce is incremented only on execution, so the transaction that schedules a recovery can be replayed after a cancellation, reinstating the recovery. Directly the revocation obligation: cancelling an authority must invalidate the signatures that established it. Contrast Candide_SocialRecoveryModule, where walletsNonces is incremented inside _executeRecovery and SES-005 is labelled enforced in D1.

findings.title: Project may fail to be deployed to chains not compatible with Shanghai hardfork
findings.mapping_rationale: solc 0.8.20 emits PUSH0, which some L2s did not support. A deployment-portability issue, and the judge questioned the Medium severity in the report itself.

findings.title: AmbireAccount implementation can be destroyed by privileges
findings.mapping_rationale: privileges set in the implementation constructor allow the reference implementation to be selfdestructed, bricking every proxy. Same class as BICONOMY-H-01; a proxy-pattern defect rather than an AA obligation.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [CL ALCHEMY-004] enforce unique deferred action nonce per UO validation (#299)
findings.mapping_rationale: deferred-action nonces were not unique per UserOperation, permitting a deferred install signature to be reused. ChainLight finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [CL ALCHEMY-003] validation function uniqueness in nonce (#293)
findings.mapping_rationale: the validation function was not uniquely determined by the nonce, so an operation could be routed to an unintended validator. ChainLight finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [CL ALCHEMY-001] validation applicability check in deferred action (#278)
findings.mapping_rationale: deferred actions skipped the check that the chosen validation is applicable to the called selector. ChainLight finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [CL ALCHEMY-002] use correct validation function for running hooks in executeUserOp (#289)
findings.mapping_rationale: execution hooks ran under the wrong validation function. ChainLight finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [QS-01] revert on presence of validation hooks in deferred validation, and run validation-associated execution hooks (#287)
findings.mapping_rationale: deferred validation did not run validation-associated execution hooks. Quantstamp finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [QS-12] prevent setting bad time ranges (#286)
findings.mapping_rationale: invalid validUntil/validAfter ranges could be installed, breaking the time bound. Quantstamp finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [Quantstamp - ALC12 & S1] fix validUntil 0 value handing in timeRangeModule (#298)
findings.mapping_rationale: validUntil of zero was mishandled in the time-range module, so a bounded key could become unbounded. Quantstamp finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [QS-ALC-4] mask deadline 48 bits (#285)
findings.mapping_rationale: the deadline was not masked to 48 bits before packing into validationData. Quantstamp finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [QS-ALC-2] add non zero address check for paymaster in modules (#279)
findings.mapping_rationale: modules accepted a zero paymaster address. Quantstamp finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [ALC-2] check paymaster address in hook as well (#309)
findings.mapping_rationale: the paymaster address was validated in one path but not in the hook path. Follow-up to QS-ALC-2.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [CL-009] address allowlist can be set independently of spend limits (#280)
findings.mapping_rationale: target allowlist and spend limit were independently settable, so a key could be scoped on one axis and unbounded on the other. ChainLight finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-100] Limit what selectors can be used by session keys on ERC-20 tokens with a spending limit (#66)
findings.mapping_rationale: session keys could invoke arbitrary selectors on ERC-20 tokens carrying a spending limit, evading the limit. Spearbit finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [quantstamp-15] only support executeWithSessionKey method in session key permission hooks (#48)
findings.mapping_rationale: session-key permission hooks applied to methods other than the intended entry point. Quantstamp finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [quantstamp-1] sessionKey ERC20 spending limit to count approve into limitUsed and ignore existing approve amount (#28)
findings.mapping_rationale: approve calls were not counted against the session key's spending limit, so a key could grant unlimited allowance. Quantstamp finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-34] Session key rotation registration check (#19)
findings.mapping_rationale: session key rotation did not re-check registration, so a rotated key could retain authority. Spearbit finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-76] Session key data storage collision (#14)
findings.mapping_rationale: session key permission data collided in storage across keys. Spearbit finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-94] runtime validation bypass special case should only allow installPlugin and upgradeToAndCall (#22)
findings.mapping_rationale: a runtime-validation bypass was broader than intended and had to be narrowed to installPlugin and upgradeToAndCall only. Spearbit finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-38] ERC-1271 signature validation with EOA owners of contract owners of MSCA (#15)
findings.mapping_rationale: ERC-1271 validation was incorrect when a contract owner itself had EOA owners. Spearbit finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-54] use salt in eip-712 domain separator (#38)
findings.mapping_rationale: the EIP-712 domain separator omitted a salt, weakening domain separation. Spearbit finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [quantstamp-3] add target is not self check in executeFromPluginExternal (#29)
findings.mapping_rationale: executeFromPluginExternal permitted calls back into the account itself, reaching privileged functions. Quantstamp finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-97] cap owners on creation to 100 (#82)
findings.mapping_rationale: owner-count cap; a DoS guard rather than an obligation.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-95][quantstamp-9] disallow self-dependencies (#33)
findings.mapping_rationale: plugin dependency cycle; not in the inventory.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [quantstamp-16] Disallow using dependencies for hooks (#77)
findings.mapping_rationale: hook dependency restriction; not in the inventory.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [quantstamp-21] prevent adding IPlugin interface to account (#45)
findings.mapping_rationale: interface-collision guard; not in the inventory.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [spearbit-51][quantstamp-14] clean up upper bits of address in PluginStorageLib (#35)
findings.mapping_rationale: dirty upper bits in packed storage; adjacent to DIG-008 but about storage, not a digest.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [S4] disable renounce ownership (#297)
findings.mapping_rationale: ownership renouncement; generic.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [S5] use Ownable2Step in AccountFactory (#296)
findings.mapping_rationale: two-step ownership; generic.

findings.commit_subject: fix: [S6][ALCHEMY-010] uninstall revert on inconsistent config (#303)
findings.mapping_rationale: uninstall did not revert on inconsistent configuration, allowing the account to reach a state with no valid validation. ChainLight finding.

findings.commit_subject: fix: added nonce to prevent signature replay (#29)
findings.mapping_rationale: an install/enable signature carried no nonce and could be replayed. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: fix: signature bypass update (#30)
findings.mapping_rationale: a signature validation bypass. Self-reported fix; subject does not describe the mechanism.

findings.commit_subject: fix: intersectValidationData to not override the aggregator (#32)
findings.mapping_rationale: validation-data intersection overwrote the aggregator field, so a failing sub-validation could be masked. Corresponds to the SECURITY CRITICAL comment now in Lib4337 L100-124.

findings.commit_subject: fix: signer cannot be address(0)
findings.mapping_rationale: a zero signer was installable, so a failed recovery returning address(0) would match. Corresponds to the guard now in ECDSAValidator L77.

findings.commit_subject: fix: check if executor is installed when executeFromExecutor is called
findings.mapping_rationale: executeFromExecutor did not verify the caller was an installed executor. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: fix: resolve signature replication issue in weighted ecdsa validator (#101)
findings.mapping_rationale: signature replication in the weighted ECDSA validator. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: fix: _setRoot to check vType (#38)
findings.mapping_rationale: setRoot did not check the validation type, permitting an inappropriate root validator. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: fix: revert before reaching postCheck (#119)
findings.mapping_rationale: execution could reach postCheck in a state where it should have reverted. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: session key validator fixed for batch scenario
findings.mapping_rationale: the session key validator did not apply policy per element in a batch. Self-reported fix; matches the SES-007 obligation and the ERC165SessionKeyValidator label in D1.

findings.commit_subject: fix: do not allow bytes20(0) on setRoot
findings.mapping_rationale: a zero root validator could be set, leaving the account with no authorisation path. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: fix Potential risk of Paymaster funds being drained
findings.mapping_rationale: unbounded paymaster sponsorship. Self-reported fix; SlowMist audit period.

findings.commit_subject: fix  Potential risks of not using real-time prices
findings.mapping_rationale: a stale or non-real-time price source was used for token conversion. Self-reported fix; matches PAY-007, which Pimlico enforces and both verifying paymasters do not.

findings.commit_subject: fix Incorrect fee amount charged
findings.mapping_rationale: the charged fee did not match the sponsored cost. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: Bugfix: Avoid attack of appending bytes to the signature
findings.mapping_rationale: trailing bytes could be appended to a signature without invalidating it. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: avoid signature length attack
findings.mapping_rationale: signature length was not constrained. Self-reported fix; earlier instance of the same class.

findings.commit_subject: Avoid `exec` re-entry attack and allowed module call `exec`
findings.mapping_rationale: re-entrancy into exec; a generic reentrancy class rather than an AA obligation.

findings.commit_subject: fix applyChange2FA operation did not check whether pending2FAAddr existed
findings.mapping_rationale: missing existence check in a 2FA change flow; project-specific, not in the inventory.

findings.commit_subject: Fix bug in `isValidSignature`
findings.mapping_rationale: an ERC-1271 validation bug. Self-reported fix; subject does not describe the mechanism.

findings.commit_subject: guardian signature bug fix
findings.mapping_rationale: a guardian signature handling bug in social recovery. Self-reported fix.

findings.commit_subject: fix : Chainlink stale checks and using 2 oracles to calculate the price
findings.mapping_rationale: stale-price checks added and a second oracle introduced. This is the change that produced the stalenessThreshold guard in BaseERC20Paymaster L215, which D1 labels PAY-007 enforced and OP-011 absent.

findings.commit_subject: fix for length & mask, pricemarkup requirement check
findings.mapping_rationale: price markup bounds enforced. Self-reported fix.
